components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1

Telephone numbers are now stored and returned in E.164 form, and the test suite passes (`./mvnw test`: 3 tests, 0 failures, BUILD SUCCESS). The suite has only those three acceptance tests, so I didn't test anything else, such as the update endpoint or the edited seed data.

**What changed**
- **`OwnerTelephone.normalize`** now:
  1. removes spaces, dashes and brackets (`()` and `[]`);
  2. keeps the country code when the number starts with `+`;
  3. otherwise drops a single leading `0` and adds `+61`;
  4. checks the result against `^\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$`, which means 8 to 15 digits after the `+`.

  Anything else, such as letters, a `+` in the middle, `+0…` or the wrong length, throws `InvalidTelephoneException`, which returns 400. For example, `0412 345 678` becomes `+61412345678`, `+64 21 123 456` becomes `+6421123456`, and `12` is rejected.
- **Duplicate check on create** now compares the E.164 values. The existing 409 error still applies.
- **Error message** now describes the E.164 rule instead of "exactly 10 digits".
- **`Owner` entity:** I replaced the old 10-digit `@Digits`/`@Pattern` checks with the E.164 pattern. Without this, Bean Validation would block saving the new values.
- **OpenAPI:** updated the `telephone` description and example.

**Three choices you may want to review**
1. **Updating an owner (PUT) also converts to E.164 now.** Before, it only accepted digits and saved them unchanged. I changed it so every saved number follows the same format; otherwise duplicate detection would be unreliable. PUT still doesn't check for duplicates, as before.
2. **Seed data:** the 10 sample owners in each database's `data.sql` (H2, HSQLDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL) had 10-digit US numbers like `6085551023`. I changed them to `+16085551023`. The new rule would have made them `+616085551023` (an Australian number), which would be wrong for Madison, WI numbers.
3. **No migration for existing databases:** any database that already holds 10-digit numbers is not converted. Those rows won't match new E.164 numbers in the duplicate check, and editing them through PUT will convert them.
